subject: general
question: What was a major focus of the 61st Constitutional Amendment?

options.text: Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats
Abolition of Privy Purses for former rulers

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the minimum voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• This amendment applied to both the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections.
 
• The purpose of the amendment was to increase the participation of younger citizens in the democratic process of the country.
 
• By enabling individuals aged 18 and above to vote, the amendment aimed to provide representation to a larger section of the population, especially the youth.
 
• The 61st Amendment reflects India's commitment to empowering its youth as active participants in decision-making and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• Constitutional amendments are changes made to the Indian Constitution to address evolving societal, political, and legal needs.
 
• They are introduced as bills in Parliament and require a special majority for approval.
 
 
 
• **Voting in India:**
 
 
• Voting is a fundamental aspect of a democracy, allowing citizens to choose their representatives.
 
• In India, voting is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• 42nd Amendment (1976): Known as the "Mini Constitution," it brought major changes like adding the words "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble.
 
• 73rd Amendment (1992): Introduced the Panchayati Raj system to strengthen local governance.
 
 
 
• **Demographics of Youth in India:**
 
 
• India has one of the largest youth populations globally, making their participation in elections critical to shaping the nation’s future.
 
• The reduced voting age allowed approximately 35 million new voters to participate in the democratic process during its initial implementation.
